mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in mortgage applications (HOUST) signals weakening household demand and housing market stress, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 declines over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a NBER-defined recession within the next 90 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion that boosts corporate earnings and risk appetite, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically greater than zero in more than 70% of triggered months, or the relationship reverses during high inflation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll growth (PAYEMS) accelerates above its 12-month moving average signals a tight labor market with upward wage pressure, which erodes corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the trigger does not precede a year-over-year CPI increase above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for three months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or inflation reaccelerates above 3% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing companies and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the trigger does not precede a decline in GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below its 12-month moving minimum signals a sharp labor market downturn, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede a NBER recession within the next 90 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 1% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion that boosts earnings and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 70% of triggered periods, or the relationship inverts during periods of high inflation (>5% CPI).
